Ligado, o DG Claw chama o Admin sozinho: When enabled, DG Claw calls the Admin automatically when an integration fails. The Admin has full access to the server, and an agent can report a failure that did not happen: this could make the Admin look into an integration that is working. The request uses fixed text, only asks for investigation and a proposal, and has limits (one per fault, one every 6 hours per integration, five per day). Nothing is applied without your approval.
Ligado: o DG Claw chama o Admin sozinho: Enabled: DG Claw calls the Admin automatically when an integration fails.
Desligado: o Admin só é chamado quando v: Disabled: the Admin is only called when you request it using the button in the integrations banner.
Estas falhas já têm correção pelo canal: These vulnerabilities already have fixes through the normal Ubuntu update channel and are not an alert. With automatic updates enabled (the Ubuntu default), the fixes are installed automatically; otherwise, use the button to ask the Admin.

Um interruptor que decide se o DG Claw c: A switch that determines whether DG Claw calls the Admin on its own when an agent integration fails (rejected key, depleted balance, unavailable system or lost connection).
Desligado de fábrica. Ligado, quando uma: Disabled by default. When enabled, if an integration fails, the Web writes a request using fixed text and delivers it to the Admin: investigate and propose, without applying anything before your approval. Limits apply: one request per fault, one every 6 hours per integration and five per day. To enable it, the screen shows the risk and asks for your confirmation.
Quem decide é você. O Admin tem acesso t: You decide. The Admin has full access to the server and an agent can report a failure that did not happen, so enabling this trades some security for speed. Disabling it takes effect immediately.
As falhas de pacotes do Ubuntu (o kernel: Vulnerabilities in Ubuntu packages (the Linux kernel, for example) that already have fixes available. They appear in one row per component, such as "Linux kernel: 12 fixes queued for the system update". Tap the row to see each vulnerability.
A cada rodada a ronda pergunta ao apt de: On each round, the security check asks this server's apt whether the fixed version can already be installed. If it can for all packages affected by the vulnerability, and the vulnerability was not in CISA's catalog of exploited vulnerabilities in the last valid check, it appears here. The row count is the number of vulnerabilities in this situation for that component. When the package is updated, the vulnerability disappears automatically.
Com a atualização automática do Ubuntu l: With Ubuntu automatic updates enabled (the default), the fix is installed automatically and you do not need to decide anything. If they are disabled, the Ask the Admin button opens the conversation with the request already written. The Admin also receives a message about these vulnerabilities and checks this. That is why they do not appear in the risk warning or badge, and remain collapsed here, in view.
